plan.area: Britain's V-force and France's Mirage IV: filling the gbr and fra heavybomber gap in js/heavyair.js
plan.diagnosis:
Measured under jsc (util, config, facts, rules, eras, heavyair, generations), not read off source lines.

THE GAP IS TOTAL. gbr heavybomber rows: 0. fra heavybomber rows: 0. Also 0 for gbr/fra stealthbomber and gunshipair, and 0 for gbr "bomber". unitFor("gbr","heavybomber",e) and unitFor("fra","heavybomber",e) return null in ALL SIX eras. The only factions with any heavybomber answer are nato (B-52, all six eras, heavyair.js), pla (H-6, e60-e20) and pact (Tu-160, e80-e20).

THE TREE ALREADY DOCUMENTS THE GAP AS A PENDING DECISION, in four places, three of which become factually false the moment rows land:
- js/eras.js:9805 "heavybomber - DELIBERATELY EMPTY, and this one is a decision awaiting the owner rather than a historical gap. The Vulcan was a real strategic bomber... Left out until the owner settles it."
- js/eras.js:10054 same for France, naming the Mirage IVA (1964) and the Mirage IVP with ASMP (1986).
- js/rules.js:2098 (fra e20) "heavybomber ... none, ever ... Restoring it means pasting back hbomber_f and the five fra_e**_heavybomber era entries."
- js/rules.js:1926 (gbr e20) "none, and none since the last Vulcan retired in 1984" - still true for e20 only.

TWO OF THE THREE V-BOMBERS ARE ALREADY IN THE GAME, AS TANKERS. gbr_e50_tanker "Valiant BK.1" (e50, radius 110, desc already cites the 1965 spar cracks); gbr_e60_tanker "Victor K.2" (e60-e80, radius 140). France's tanker leg is there too: fra_e60_tanker "C-135F", then C-135FR at e80/e90/e00. So the Mirage IV's short legs already have their answer on the roster.

MECHANISMS THAT DECIDE THE DESIGN, all measured:
1. unitFor() returns exactly ONE unit per faction+role+era (rules.js:4259) and every caller in game.js and ai.js uses it, never unitsFor(). So one British bomber per band - the Victor cannot share e50 with the Valiant or e60 with the Vulcan.
2. generations.js:902 POOL floors every heavybomber's ammo at 6. Measured: pla_e60_heavybomber is written ammo:5 and resolves to 6; pla_e80 is written ammo:2 and resolves to 6. Any new row written below 6 is silently rewritten, so the per-sortie limit must live in the WEAPON's ammo cost, not the pool.
3. generations.js DOMAIN includes gbr and fra, so their weapons are cloned and rescaled. Verified on the patched tree: yellowsun2 acc 0.64 -> 0.641 (gbr optics 1.02 at e60 bite 0.10), an22 0.68 -> 0.678 (fra optics 0.94), asmp 0.88 -> 0.898 (fra guided 1.06 - the French missile bonus landing on the French missile). bluedanube is untouched because DOMAIN_BITE.e50 is 0.00.
4. Nuclear release already exists, and `nuke:true` is the WRONG flag: holdsFire() (entities.js:518) demands a bombard order carrying nuke:true, raised only by the superweapon path in ui.js, so a bomb setting it could never fire. The right flag is `manual`, used by all eleven held rounds in the game (every srbm_*, every ARM); entities.js:244 stamps release onto any attack or bombard order, so naming a target IS the release.
5. `rounds` is not usable here: zero air units in the roster carry it, and entities.js:480 would put an airborne unit on the ground resupply clock.
6. render3d.js modelKeyFor() falls back to a same-role peer's mesh, and air_specs.js AIRFRAMES has no gbr or fra row at all - so without new AIRFRAMES rows every British and French bomber would fly as a B-52.

RANGE CONTEXT, measured from the resolved tree: the longest air-defence reach is 10.6 tiles in e50/e60, 12.5 in e80/e90, 13.6 in e00/e20. The B-52's stand-off rounds sit at 11.5/13.0/15.0/16.0 against those. Free-fall rounds in this file sit at 2.2.
plan.summary:
Five new rows and five new weapons in js/heavyair.js, five silhouettes in js/air_specs.js, and four stale comments corrected.

BRITAIN - gbr_e50 Valiant B.1 (Blue Danube), gbr_e60 Vulcan B.2 (Yellow Sun Mk.2), gbr_e80 Vulcan B.2 (Black Buck, 21 x 1,000 lb). e90, e00, e20 EMPTY and permanently so.
FRANCE - fra_e60 Mirage IVA (AN-22), fra_e80 Mirage IVP (ASMP), the second running from:"e80" to:"e90". e50, e00, e20 EMPTY.

The three V-bombers are deliberately NOT three identical rows. The Valiant is first in (Feb 1955), the only one that bombed in anger (Suez 1956), and the only one whose row STOPS at e50 - the rear-spar cracks grounded the fleet on 26 January 1965. The Vulcan is the only airframe in the file to appear twice for two different jobs, megaton free-fall at e60 and iron bombs at e80. The Victor gets NO bomber row, and that is the answer rather than an omission: its bomber career (Nov 1957 - 31 Dec 1968) sits entirely inside two bands already held by an aircraft that arrived first and left later, unitFor() returns one airframe per band, and the game already carries the Victor in the role it actually ended in - gbr_e60_tanker, Victor K.2, e60-e80, the aircraft that refuelled Black Buck.

The British arc is deliberately FLAT where the American one climbs: all three British rounds sit at 2.2 tiles, because Britain never fielded a stand-off weapon that worked (Blue Steel 1963 reached ~100 nmi, inside the belt; Skybolt cancelled Dec 1962; Blue Streak cancelled 1960). That is why the deterrent went to sea in 1969, which this game already models as gbr_e60_ssbn. France is the contrast: ASMP at 10.4 tiles in 1986 is the weapon Britain was refused, arriving twenty-two years after the aeroplane.

Nuclear rounds use `manual: true` (release only on an order), ammo 6 against a pool of 6 = one weapon per sortie. Black Buck's conventional load is NOT manual - an iron bomb needs no release authority - and carries the worst accuracy figure in the file, because XM607 put one bomb of twenty-one on the runway.

Verified on patched copies under jsc: 0 dangling weapon ids across all 1,207 units; the full faction x role x era unitFor snapshot diff is exactly 6 changed lines, +5 units, +9 weapons (5 base + 4 DOMAIN clones). Nothing else in the roster moves.
plan.sources:
Service dates, payloads, ranges and weapons, all cited in the code comments themselves:
VALIANT - first flight 18 May 1951; 138 Sqn RAF Gaydon Feb 1955, first V-bomber in service; 104 built; 21,000 lb / 21 x 1,000 lb bomb load; 567 mph at 30,000 ft; Suez conventional raids Oct-Nov 1956 (the only V-bomber to bomb in anger); dropped Britain's first atomic weapon, a Blue Danube, at Maralinga 11 Oct 1956 (Op Buffalo) and the first British hydrogen bomb over Christmas Island 15 May 1957 (Op Grapple); rear-spar fatigue found 1964, fleet grounded 26 Jan 1965.
VULCAN - first flight 30 Aug 1952; B.1 with 83 Sqn Waddington July 1956; B.2 with 83 Sqn 1 July 1960; 136 built; 21,000 lb bomb load; Mach 0.96 / 645 mph; combat range ~4,830 km; Black Buck 1, XM607 of 44 Sqn, Ascension, 30 April - 1 May 1982, 3,900 nmi each way, 11 Victor K.2 tankers, 18 refuellings, 21 x 1,000 lb across the Port Stanley runway at 30 degrees, one hit; 44 Sqn disbanded 21 Dec 1982; 50 Sqn's Vulcan K.2 tankers to 31 March 1984.
VICTOR - first flight 24 Dec 1952; deliveries from Nov 1957, 10 Sqn 1958; 86 built; 35 x 1,000 lb, the largest conventional load of the three; B.2 with Blue Steel from Feb 1962; Blue Steel force stood down 31 Dec 1968; K.1 tankers from 1965 after the Valiant grounding, K.2 from 1974, retired 15 Oct 1993.
WEAPONS - Blue Danube, Britain's first operational nuclear weapon, in service Nov 1953, ~10,000 lb, 62 in diameter, ~10-12 kt, ~58 built. Yellow Sun Mk.2, in service 1961, 7,250 lb, Red Snow warhead ~1.1 Mt, ~150 built, carried by Vulcan and Victor. Blue Steel, in service Feb 1963, ~100 nmi, Mach 2.3, Red Snow warhead, withdrawn 1970. Skybolt cancelled by the US Dec 1962 (Nassau); Blue Streak cancelled 1960. Polaris: RN took the deterrent 30 June 1969.
MIRAGE IV - prototype first flight 17 June 1959; production IVA first flight 7 Dec 1963; EB 1/91 Gascogne, Mont-de-Marsan, 1 October 1964; 62 production aircraft; two crew; 23.5 m long, 11.85 m span; Mach 2.2; combat radius ~1,240 km hi-lo-hi; twelve C-135F bought 1964 plus Mirage-on-Mirage buddy refuelling. AN-11 60 kt from 1964, AN-22 70 kt from 1967, ~700 kg, carried semi-recessed. Mirage IVP: 18 converted, in service 1 May 1986, one ASMP - ramjet, Mach 3, TN 81 warhead 300 kt, 80 km from low level to ~300 km from altitude. Strike role ended 1 July 1996 (passed to Mirage 2000N, later Rafale B); the survivors flew strategic reconnaissance to 23 June 2005. First French warhead: Gerboise Bleue, Reggane, 13 February 1960.
In-tree cross-checks used for calibration: rules.js slbm_polaris (dmg 700, aoe 4.4) and slbm_m20 (680, 4.4) set the scale for a strategic nuclear round modelled conventionally; heavyair.js ironbombs / bigbelly / h6_bombs set the free-fall idiom; rules.js FIXED_MAGAZINE, entities.js manualWeapon()/holdsFire()/airBurn(), generations.js POOL and DOMAIN set the mechanics.

edits.why: Documents the two new families in the file's own voice, says which era bands are EMPTY and why, and records that the Victor's absence from the bomber rows is a decision with a reason rather than an oversight. Anchored on the last line of the existing header, which is unique despite the two duplicated H-6 paragraphs above it.

edits.newCode:
THE V-FORCE. Valiant, Vulcan, Victor - Britain's deterrent from 1955 until
   the Royal Navy took it to sea with Polaris on 30 June 1969, a handover this
   game already models on the submarine side as gbr_e60_ssbn, HMS Resolution.
   They were not three interchangeable aeroplanes and they do not get three
   interchangeable rows:
     VALIANT, 138 Squadron at Gaydon, February 1955 - the first of the three,
     104 built, and the only V-bomber that ever bombed in anger, over Egyptian
     airfields at Suez in October 1956. It dropped Britain's first atomic bomb
     at Maralinga on 11 October 1956 and the first British hydrogen bomb over
     Christmas Island on 15 May 1957. Fatigue cracks in the rear spar grounded
     the fleet on 26 January 1965, so its row is `to: "e50"` and stops.
     VULCAN B.2 holds e60 AND e80 - the only airframe here that appears twice
     for two different jobs. 1960: a megaton bomb it must fly over the target
     to release. 1982: twenty-one 1,000 lb bombs on Port Stanley, and it still
     must fly over the target. Twenty-seven years and the problem never moved.
     VICTOR gets NO bomber row, and that is an answer rather than a gap. Its
     bomber career, November 1957 to 31 December 1968, sits entirely inside two
     bands already held by an aircraft that arrived first and left later, and
     unitFor() returns exactly ONE airframe per faction, role and era. What the
     Victor is in this game is what it became: gbr_e60_tanker, Victor K.2,
     e60 to e80. Eleven of them refuelled the one Vulcan that flew Black Buck.
   So Britain's arc is FLAT where the American one climbs. The B-52 escapes the
   overflight problem in 1982 and never goes back; the V-force never escapes it.
   Blue Steel reached about 100 nautical miles from 1963 - inside the belt it
   was meant to defeat - Skybolt was cancelled by Washington in December 1962
   and Blue Streak in 1960. That is why the ranges below do not move.

   MIRAGE IV. The airborne leg of the force de frappe, and the one nation here
   that built the whole chain itself: aeroplane, warhead, missile and the
   tanker doctrine to reach with it. Prototype 17 June 1959; EB 1/91 Gascogne
   at Mont-de-Marsan on 1 October 1964; 62 production aircraft. It is not a
   strategic bomber in the B-52 sense and the figures say so: a Mach 2.2
   two-seat delta the size of a large fighter with a combat radius near
   1,240 km, which is why France bought twelve C-135F the same year and
   practised Mirage-on-Mirage buddy tanking. The reach belongs to
   fra_e60_tanker, not to the bomber.
   e50 EMPTY: no French warhead until Reggane, 13 February 1960, and nothing to
   drop one from until 1964. e00 and e20 EMPTY: the strike role left this
   aeroplane on 1 July 1996 for the Mirage 2000N and later the Rafale B, both
   already on the French roster as fighters; the last eighteen airframes flew
   strategic RECONNAISSANCE, not strike, until 23 June 2005.


   Loaded after eras.js so it can add to the roster and reindex.            */

sfx: "missile", profile: "loft", intercept: 0.40 },

    /* ---- what the V-force carried ----
       All three are free-fall at the same 2.2 tiles as the B-52D's and the
       H-6A's, and that is the point rather than an oversight: Britain never
       fielded a stand-off round that worked. Blue Steel of 1963 reached about
       100 nautical miles against an e60 area SAM this game gives 10.6 tiles,
       Skybolt was cancelled in December 1962 and Blue Streak in 1960, so there
       is no British `alcm_b` to write.

       `manual`, NOT `nuke`. The nuke flag needs a bombard order carrying
       nuke:true, which ui.js raises only for the superweapon, so a bomb that
       set it could never be released at all. `manual` is the flag the eleven
       held rounds already in the game use - every srbm_* and every ARM - and
       entities.js:244 stamps release onto any attack or bombard order, so a
       player or the AI naming a target IS the release. Left alone the
       aeroplane holds the weapon, which is correct for a bomb that needed the
       Prime Minister.

       `ammo: 6` against a pool of 6 on each airframe: ONE weapon a sortie,
       then home. 6 rather than 1 because generations.js:902 floors every
       heavybomber's pool at 6 and would otherwise hand a Valiant six Blue
       Danubes. About 58 were built and the RAF loaded one per aircraft. */
    bluedanube: { name: "Blue Danube free-fall bomb", dmg: 520, warhead: "he",
                  range: 2.2, reload: 6.0, burst: 1, acc: 0.66, proj: "bomb",
                  speed: 0, aoe: 3.6, suppress: 260, ammo: 6, manual: true,
                  tgt: { ground: 1, air: 0, sea: 1, sub: 0 } },
    /* Yellow Sun Mk.2, in service 1961: 7,250 lb, the Red Snow warhead, about
       1.1 megatons against Blue Danube's ten kilotons. A hundredfold in life
       and a forty-per-cent step here, compressed the way this file already
       compresses range - the ORDER is what has to survive. */
    yellowsun2: { name: "Yellow Sun Mk.2 free-fall bomb", dmg: 720, warhead: "he",
                  range: 2.2, reload: 6.5, burst: 1, acc: 0.64, proj: "bomb",
                  speed: 0, aoe: 4.6, suppress: 300, ammo: 6, manual: true,
                  tgt: { ground: 1, air: 0, sea: 1, sub: 0 } },
    /* Black Buck: the Vulcan's full conventional bay, twenty-one 1,000 lb
       bombs as three sticks of seven - ammo 2 against a pool of 6. NOT manual;
       an iron bomb needs no release authority. The accuracy is deliberately
       the worst bomb figure in the file: XM607 laid all twenty-one across the
       Port Stanley runway at a 30-degree angle on 1 May 1982 and put exactly
       ONE of them on it. */
    blackbuck:  { name: "21 x 1,000lb bomb load", dmg: 140, warhead: "he",
                  range: 2.2, reload: 1.0, burst: 7, burstDelay: 0.20, acc: 0.55,
                  proj: "bomb", speed: 0, aoe: 3.4, suppress: 160, ammo: 2,
                  tgt: { ground: 1, air: 0, sea: 1, sub: 0 } },

    /* ---- what the Mirage IV carried ----
       AN-22, in service 1967: a 70-kiloton boosted-fission bomb of about
       700 kg carried semi-recessed in a belly fairing, replacing the 60 kt
       AN-11 the aircraft entered service with in 1964. One bomb, one aircraft,
       and it has to be overhead - the same problem the V-force never solved,
       met by a country that solved it nineteen years later. */
    an22:       { name: "AN-22 free-fall bomb", dmg: 600, warhead: "he",
                  range: 2.0, reload: 6.0, burst: 1, acc: 0.68, proj: "bomb",
                  speed: 0, aoe: 4.0, suppress: 280, ammo: 6, manual: true,
                  tgt: { ground: 1, air: 0, sea: 1, sub: 0 } },
    /* ASMP - Air-Sol Moyenne Portee - on the Mirage IVP from 1 May 1986: a
       ramjet at Mach 3 with the 300 kt TN 81, 80 km from low level and up to
       300 km from altitude. This is the weapon Britain wanted and was refused,
       and it arrives twenty-two years after the aeroplane did. 10.4 tiles puts
       it just outside the 10.6-tile area SAM of e60 and just inside the 12.5
       of e80, which is honest: a stand-off weapon against last decade's
       defences.
       sea:0 is deliberate and is not a handicap. ASMP is a strategic land
       attack round and France never fitted it for anti-ship work; the French
       anti-ship weapon is Exocet and it is already on the rows that carry it.
       intercept 0.30 because a Mach 3 ramjet is a hard shot. */
    asmp:       { name: "ASMP stand-off missile", dmg: 660, warhead: "he",
                  range: 10.4, minRange: 2.5, reload: 9.0, burst: 1, acc: 0.88,
                  proj: "missile", speed: 420, aoe: 4.2, suppress: 200, ammo: 6,
                  manual: true, tgt: { ground: 1, air: 0, sea: 0, sub: 0 },
                  sfx: "missile", profile: "loft", intercept: 0.30 },
  };

/* ---- THE V-FORCE: three aeroplanes, three different endings ----
       e90, e00 and e20 are EMPTY and stay empty. No. 44 Squadron, the last
       Vulcan bomber squadron, disbanded on 21 December 1982 and No. 50's
       Vulcan K.2 tankers went on 31 March 1984. */
    gbr_e50_heavybomber: vforce({
      name: "Valiant B.1", full: "Vickers Valiant B.1 with Blue Danube",
      /* 138 Squadron, RAF Gaydon, February 1955; 104 built; 567 mph at
         30,000 ft, slightly slower than a B-52D so 4.4 against its 4.6.
         Radius 78 against the Buff's 96. gbr_e50_tanker is the SAME airframe
         at 110, and that is right rather than a contradiction: the BK.1 threw
         the bomb bay away and filled the aeroplane with fuel. */
      cost: 3000, oil: 85, time: 42, hp: 760, speed: 4.4, ammo: 6, radius: 78,
      rcs: 5.0, turn: 0.6,
      weapons: ["bluedanube"], from: "e50", to: "e50",
      service: "1955", confidence: "high",
      desc: "The first of the three, and the only V-bomber that ever bombed in " +
            "anger - Egyptian airfields, October 1956. It dropped Britain's first " +
            "atomic bomb at Maralinga on 11 October 1956 and the first British " +
            "hydrogen bomb over Christmas Island on 15 May 1957. One weapon a " +
            "sortie, and it must be directly overhead to release it. Fatigue " +
            "cracks in the rear spar grounded the fleet on 26 January 1965, which " +
            "is why this row does not run on into the next decade." }),
    gbr_e60_heavybomber: vforce({
      name: "Vulcan B.2", full: "Avro Vulcan B.2 with Yellow Sun Mk.2",
      /* B.2 with 83 Squadron on 1 July 1960; 136 Vulcans built; Mach 0.96 and
         645 mph, the fastest of the three, so 4.9. Combat range about
         4,830 km gives 86 tiles. A delta rolls better than a Buff. */
      cost: 3400, oil: 94, time: 46, hp: 820, speed: 4.9, ammo: 6, radius: 86,
      rcs: 5.4, turn: 0.75, r: 27, gen: 2.5,
      weapons: ["yellowsun2"], from: "e60", to: "e60",
      service: "1960", confidence: "high",
      desc: "Britain's deterrent in one aeroplane: a megaton bomb in a delta " +
            "wing at 56,000 feet, held until an order names the target. What it " +
            "has no way of doing is releasing from outside the missile belt. " +
            "Blue Steel reached a hundred miles from 1963 and that was not far " +
            "enough; Skybolt was cancelled by Washington in December 1962. The " +
            "deterrent went to sea with Polaris on 30 June 1969 for exactly this " +
            "reason, and the submarine that took it is already on this roster." }),
    gbr_e80_heavybomber: vforce({
      name: "Vulcan B.2 (Black Buck)", full: "Avro Vulcan B.2, conventional fit",
      /* Same airframe, same radius, conventional bay. The reach that made
         Black Buck possible was not in the aeroplane: XM607 flew 3,900
         nautical miles from Ascension on 30 April 1982 on eleven Victor K.2
         tankers and eighteen refuellings, and gbr_e60_tanker covers e80. */
      cost: 3300, oil: 92, time: 45, hp: 820, speed: 4.9, ammo: 6, radius: 86,
      rcs: 5.4, turn: 0.75, r: 27, gen: 2.5,
      weapons: ["blackbuck"], from: "e80", to: "e80",
      service: "1982", confidence: "high",
      desc: "Twenty-seven years old, retired on paper, and sent 3,900 miles to " +
            "bomb a runway because nothing else could reach it. Twenty-one " +
            "thousand-pounders in three sticks and an aiming error measured in " +
            "hundreds of yards - one bomb of twenty-one hit. It cannot get there " +
            "without a tanker, and the tanker on this roster is the third " +
            "V-bomber. The last squadron disbanded on 21 December 1982." }),

    /* ---- MIRAGE IV: the force de frappe, built end to end in France ----
       e50 EMPTY - no French warhead until 13 February 1960 and no aircraft to
       carry one until 1964. e00 and e20 EMPTY - the strike role left this
       aeroplane on 1 July 1996 for the Mirage 2000N and then the Rafale B,
       which are fighters and are already on the French roster as fighters. */
    fra_e60_heavybomber: mirage4({
      name: "Mirage IVA", full: "Dassault Mirage IVA with the AN-22 bomb",
      /* EB 1/91 Gascogne, Mont-de-Marsan, 1 October 1964; 62 built; Mach 2.2,
         so 7.6 - by a wide margin the fastest aircraft in this file and faster
         than most fighters of its own decade. Radius 46 against a Vulcan's 86:
         about 1,240 km hi-lo-hi, which does not reach Moscow and was never
         expected to without the C-135F. */
      cost: 2800, oil: 74, time: 40, hp: 520, speed: 7.6, ammo: 6, radius: 46,
      weapons: ["an22"], from: "e60", to: "e60",
      service: "1964", confidence: "high",
      desc: "France's own bomb on France's own aeroplane, refuelled by France's " +
            "own doctrine - twelve C-135F bought in 1964 and Mirage-on-Mirage " +
            "buddy tanking for the rest. Mach 2.2 and half the size of a " +
            "V-bomber, which buys speed and costs range: on internal fuel it " +
            "reaches about 1,240 km and no further. Two crew, one 70-kiloton " +
            "bomb under the belly, and it has to fly over the target." }),
    fra_e80_heavybomber: mirage4({
      name: "Mirage IVP", full: "Dassault Mirage IVP with ASMP",
      /* Eighteen converted; EB 1/91 again, 1 May 1986. The row runs to e90
         because the strike role did: it ended on 1 July 1996, inside the 1990s
         band, and the survivors flew reconnaissance only until 2005. */
      cost: 3000, oil: 76, time: 42, hp: 540, speed: 7.6, ammo: 6, radius: 46,
      radarQ: 3, gen: 3.5,
      weapons: ["asmp"], from: "e80", to: "e90",
      service: "1986", confidence: "high",
      desc: "Eighteen airframes rebuilt around one missile. ASMP is a Mach 3 " +
            "ramjet with a 300-kiloton warhead that flies up to 300 km on its " +
            "own, so for the first time the aeroplane launches and turns away " +
            "instead of flying over. Britain wanted this in 1962, was refused " +
            "Skybolt and gave up; France built it and waited twenty-two years. " +
            "The strike role ended on 1 July 1996 and passed to the fighters." }),

    /* ---- C-130: the airlifter ---- */

risks: THE AI WILL NOW BUILD THEM. ai.js calls unitFor(P.faction, role, P.era) in five places and the heavybomber role previously answered null for gbr and fra, which cooled the role. A British or French AI in e50-e90 can now put a bomber in its build mix. That is a real behaviour change and it is the single most likely cause if the 89/0 suite moves. Measure it before anything else.

HELD ROUNDS AND THE AI. Four of the five rows carry only a `manual` weapon, so the aircraft fires nothing at all unless an order names a target. entities.js:244 stamps release onto attack and bombard orders, and ai.js issues those, so this should work - but the precedent is all GROUND launchers (every tel_*), and no AIRCRAFT in the roster has ever carried a held round before. If an AI-built Vulcan orbits without dropping, that is where to look. The three TEL rows prove the gate itself works; they do not prove it works from an airborne platform.

THE VICTOR GETS NO BOMBER ROW. This is a design decision, not an oversight, and the owner may disagree with it. unitFor() returns one airframe per faction, role and era, so a Victor bomber row could only exist by displacing the Valiant at e50 (in service three years earlier, and the aircraft that actually dropped Blue Danube and bombed Suez) or the Vulcan at e60 (which held the role nine years longer). If the owner wants the Victor visible as a bomber, the honest way is a new era band, not a second row in an occupied one.

heavyair.js IS ALREADY DUPLICATED, and I did not touch it. The badger() helper is defined twice (lines 181-187 and 193-199), the three pla_e**_heavybomber rows appear twice (305-335 and 342-372), and the H-6 header paragraph appears twice (18-29 and 32-43). The second definition wins in each case and the values are identical, so it is inert - but every anchor I chose was checked for uniqueness against this, and any future anchor in that file must be too.

THE MAG BLOCK AT heavyair.js:415 IS DEAD CODE and I left it alone. It sets UNITS[id].magazine to a NUMBER (1, 2), while entities.js:1583 reads this.def.magazine[this.def.weapons[wi]] - indexing a number by a string, which is undefined, so the branch never runs. rules.js FIXED_MAGAZINE keys by weapon id. None of my rows are in MAG so nothing here changes, but it is worth a separate fix and is out of scope for this stream.

THE ttail DOUBLE-TAILPLANE. addTail() in air3d_era.js draws a fin-top stabiliser in its ttail branch and then falls through to `if (P.htail !== "none") stab(...)`, so the six existing rows written tail:"ttail" + htail:"high" get a spurious second low tailplane. I avoided it on the Valiant with htail:"none" and said why in the comment. I did NOT fix the six existing rows - that is a separate change and would alter six aircraft nobody asked me to touch.

COMPRESSED YIELDS. Blue Danube is ~10 kt and Yellow Sun Mk.2 is ~1.1 Mt - a hundredfold - and they are written 520 and 720, a forty-per-cent step. That is the same kind of compression this codebase already applies to range (generations.js R(), exponent 0.45) and to slbm_polaris at dmg 700, and the ORDER is preserved, but it is compression and the comment says so rather than pretending otherwise.

ASMP CARRIES sea:0, so fra_e80_heavybomber cannot engage a ship at all. That is deliberate and historical - ASMP is a strategic land-attack round, France's anti-ship weapon is Exocet - but it means the French bomber is useless in a purely naval scenario. If that reads as a bug to a player rather than a fact, the card text is where to fix it, not the tgt mask.

problems.item: AI release of the held nuclear round (design claim: `manual` = the Prime Minister's authority)
problems.claim: heavyair.js weapon comment and diagnosis point 4: "`manual` is the flag the eleven held rounds already in the game use ... a player or the AI naming a target IS the release. Left alone the aeroplane holds the weapon, which is correct for a bomb that needed the Prime Minister."
problems.reality: For the AI the gate is decorative and it will be spent on ore trucks. Measured path: ai.js:3959-4021 sweeps every idle airframe; pickAirTarget (ai.js:5310) is TERMINAL only for role sead/ewair, and heavybomber is neither fighter nor cas, so it falls into the gunship branch at ai.js:5336 `if (!(e.def.harvester || e.armor === "heavy")) continue;` and returns the nearest harvester or heavy-armour contact; ai.js:4006 then issues `a.give({type:"attack", target: tgt})` with no `auto`, so entities.js:244 stamps release and holdsFire() drops. A gbr or fra AI in e50-e90 therefore puts its one-per-sortie Blue Danube / Yellow Sun Mk.2 / AN-22 (dmg 520/720/600, aoe 3.6/4.6/4.0) into a harvester. The report's own precedent comment at ai.js:5310 was written to stop exactly this for HARM and was not extended to the new role. Not mentioned anywhere in the report.

problems.item: Release authority does not survive a tanker cycle - the failure mode the Mirage IV is most exposed to
problems.claim: risks: "entities.js:244 stamps release onto attack and bombard orders, and ai.js issues those, so this should work"; and the fra design leans on fra_e60_tanker: "The reach belongs to fra_e60_tanker, not to the bomber."
problems.reality: release is lost the moment the aircraft breaks off to a boom. entities.js:2004-2009 builds the carried-across strike as `{ type: "attack", target: o.target, resume: o.resume, cap: o.cap, auto: o.auto }` - no `release` - and every hand-back assigns it straight to this.order (entities.js:2253, 2266, 2282, 2296) rather than through setOrder(), which is the ONLY place release is stamped (entities.js:243-244). On the resumed leg released() is false, holdsFire() is true, pickWeapon skips the only mount (entities.js:1532), updateAir's attack branch takes `wi < 0` and calls afterAttack(o), which for an all-held airframe ends at attackmove/hover. Net: the aircraft burns a full tanker load, flies back to the target and drops nothing. gbr_e50/gbr_e60 and fra_e60/fra_e80 are all-manual (measured) and all are flagged refuelable by heavyair.js's own re-derivation; the Mirage IV at radius 46 is the most likely aircraft in the game to hit bingo before weapon release. The bug pre-exists for SEAD, but SEAD shoots at 0.88 x 10.5 tiles and rarely reaches it; a 2.0-2.2 tile free-fall bomber reaches it routinely.

problems.item: risks item 2: "no AIRCRAFT in the roster has ever carried a held round before"
problems.claim: "the precedent is all GROUND launchers (every tel_*), and no AIRCRAFT in the roster has ever carried a held round before ... The three TEL rows prove the gate itself works; they do not prove it works from an airborne platform."
problems.reality: False, and it contradicts the report's own diagnosis point 4 ("every ARM"). Measured on the unpatched tree: 6 aircraft carry a weapon-level `manual` round (sead_n, sead_g, sead_c, sead_p, ew_n, ew_c - all allManual) and 34 aircraft carry def.noAuto, which manualWeapon() treats identically (entities.js:503) - including gbr's own ew_b. The airborne precedent is large and already tested by _behtest [7]/the Weasel cases at lines 1024-1075. The claim only matters because it makes the risk look larger than it is while hiding the two real holes above.

problems.item: ui.js refusal text for an all-held aircraft is SEAD-specific
problems.claim: Not addressed by the report at all.
problems.reality: ui.js:1071-1081: right-clicking bare ground with an all-held aircraft selected refuses with "n HELD - RIGHT-CLICK THE EMITTER, NOT THE GROUND". Four of the five new rows are allWeaponsHeld() = true (measured), so a player who selects a Valiant, a Vulcan B.2 or a Mirage IVA and clicks the ground is told to right-click an emitter by an aeroplane carrying a free-fall atomic bomb and no anti-radiation round. Same class of wording problem in entities.js:2071's `defenceless` branch, which now routes the V-force around every seen SAM ring on move/cap/attackmove - defensible, but the report claims the British arc is "it must fly over the target" and never says the aircraft will refuse to approach unless the order names a target.

problems.item: New comment text asserts roster facts that are not true of this roster (edits 6 and 8)
problems.claim: eras.js replacement: "the strike role left this aeroplane on 1 July 1996 for the Mirage 2000N and later the Rafale B, both of which are on this roster as fighters". rules.js replacement: "bomber_f already covers that airframe in the role it actually flies."
problems.reality: Measured under jsc: there is no Mirage 2000N anywhere in UNITS (fra e90 cas = fra_e90_cas "Mirage 2000D"; fra e80/e90 sead = Jaguar A / ARMAT). The Rafale rows are fra_e00_fighter "Rafale" and fighter_f "Rafale" (role fighter) plus fra_e00_cas "Rafale / AASM" (role cas) - so "both ... as fighters" is wrong for one of the two named aircraft and the other does not exist. bomber_f is "Mirage 2000D RMV", role cas, fac fra - it is not the Rafale B airframe the sentence is about. There is also no role named "bomber" in the game at all (0 rows in the full role sweep). These four edits exist solely to stop stale comments misleading the next reader; replacing them with new false statements about ids that can be grepped is the same defect in the other direction.

problems.item: Diagnosis point 4, the mechanism attributed to the `nuke` flag
problems.claim: "holdsFire() (entities.js:518) demands a bombard order carrying nuke:true, raised only by the superweapon path in ui.js, so a bomb setting it could never fire."
problems.reality: The conclusion is right and the reason is stronger than stated: NOTHING raises it. grep across js/ finds `nuke` as an order property nowhere - ui.js has it only as a CSS class and a label (ui.js:2511, 2535), ai.js not at all, and the only `nuke:true` in the roster is the silo round at rules.js:1499, with game.js:1317/1386 passing it as an areaStrike option. entities.js:516-521's own comment ("a token written in exactly two places, the two-stage confirmation in ui.js and driveNuclear() in ai.js") is itself stale - driveNuclear does not exist in ai.js. Worth correcting rather than repeating, since the new weapon comment repeats the ui.js claim verbatim.

problems.item: Range-context figure for e20
problems.claim: "the longest air-defence reach is 10.6 tiles in e50/e60, 12.5 in e80/e90, 13.6 in e00/e20."
problems.reality: Measured over every faction/role/era resolved loadout: e50 10.6 (gbr_e50_sam), e60 10.6, e80 12.5, e90 12.5, e00 13.6 (nato_e00_sam), e20 15.0 (destroyer_b, Aster 30). 13.6 is the e00 figure only. Nothing in the patch depends on it - no new row reaches e20 - but the same sentence is the justification offered for ASMP at 10.4, so the survey it comes from should be right.

problems.item: Diagnosis roster survey of who already answers heavybomber
problems.claim: "The only factions with any heavybomber answer are nato (B-52, all six eras), pla (H-6, e60-e20) and pact (Tu-160, e80-e20)."
problems.reality: Measured: pact|heavybomber resolves to pact_e80_stealthbomber for e80/e90/e00 and sbomber_p for e20; pla|heavybomber|e20 resolves to sbomber_c, not an H-6. The pact and e20 pla answers are stealth-bomber rows standing in, not Tu-160/H-6 heavybomber rows. Cosmetic, but the survey is the evidence offered for "the gap is total".

missed: THE SUITE CANNOT MOVE, and the report should say so instead of asking the human to find out. _behtest.html:335-338 forces opt-era and opt-aera to "e20" before pressing start, and the patch adds nothing at e20: measured unitFor("gbr","heavybomber","e20") and unitFor("fra","heavybomber","e20") both stay "-". No test iterates UNITS or ROLES, and the only unitFor calls in the harness are lines 454 and 482 (role "fighter") and 541 (role "aa"). So risk 1 ("the single most likely cause if the 89/0 suite moves") cannot fire in the suite at all - it fires in a real e50-e90 match, which is the thing that actually needs measuring.

ALL NINE ANCHORS VERIFIED count = 1 with python3 str.count against the live files, and the insert fault is NOT present: all five inserts repeat the anchored text (edit 1 at the foot, edit 2 at head AND foot - both lines of its two-line anchor survive - edits 3, 4, 5 at the foot, edit 9 at the head). Applied to copies, all four patched files contain zero `,\s*,` sequences and the whole tree parses under jsc.

RESOLVED-TREE MEASUREMENTS ALL REPRODUCE. Full faction x role x era unitFor snapshot diff is exactly 16 lines: the 6 changed unitFor rows the report predicts, UNITCOUNT 1202 -> 1207, WEAPONCOUNT 1784 -> 1793, dangling 0 before and after. Per-row figures match section 4 to the digit, including the DOMAIN clone suffixes (yellowsun2__gbr_e60_heavybomber acc 0.641, blackbuck__gbr_e80_heavybomber 0.552, an22__fra_e60_heavybomber 0.678, asmp__fra_e80_heavybomber 0.898) and bluedanube staying uncloned at e50, every pool floored to exactly 6 by generations.js:902, and fra_e80's sight self-grown to 10.7.

MODELS CHECK OUT. air_specs.js rows go in before the registerAll() call at air_specs.js:267, AIRFRAMES 131 -> 136 and all five new keys register into UNIT_MODELS by unit id (air3d_era.js:1507-1522), which is exactly the key modelKeyFor (render3d.js:309) asks for first - so the B-52 fallback the report warns about is genuinely closed. Every token used exists: BODY.area is a real entry (air3d_era.js, the area-ruled 1950s waist), PAINT has silver/white/green/seagrey, intake "cheek" has its own branch, and engMount "wing" + intake "wingroot" correctly falls through to the buried-nozzle branch (air3d_era.js:636) while addIntakes returns early at :656 so no duplicate duct is hung. The ttail fall-through the report describes is real - addTail's ttail branch does not return and the trailing `if (P.htail !== "none") stab(...)` would add a second low tailplane - so htail:"none" on the Valiant is correct. Nothing is allocated per frame: build() runs once per key and getModel caches by key|team.

heavyair.js's MAG block being dead (entities.js:1583 indexes a NUMBER by a weapon-id string) is correctly reported and is genuinely inert for these rows. Also confirmed inert: the duplicated badger() definition and the duplicated pla_e60/e80/e00_heavybomber keys in NEW - identical values, last one wins - and the C-130 anchor is still unique despite them.

A CONSEQUENCE THE REPORT DOES NOT DRAW: because 4 of the 5 rows are allWeaponsHeld(), ai.js:4021 refuses to fly them on an armed sweep (the `if (a.def.jam)` escape does not apply), so an AI bomber only ever launches when pickAirTarget already holds something - which, per problem 1, is a harvester. The e80 Black Buck Vulcan is the opposite case: its round is not manual, so it alone sweeps and acquires normally. That asymmetry between the two Vulcan rows is a real behavioural split worth stating in the file's own voice, since the comment presents them as the same aeroplane doing the same job twenty-seven years apart.

If the two majors are to be fixed rather than documented: (a) give pickAirTarget a terminal branch for role "heavybomber" the way it already has one for sead/ewair, so a held strategic round is never auto-aimed at a harvester; (b) carry `release: o.release` in the entities.js:2004-2009 resume literal (or route the hand-backs at 2253/2266/2282/2296 through setOrder), which also repairs the pre-existing SEAD case. Neither touches the roster rows and neither is in the report's edit list.

problems.item: js/heavyair.js — the British design thesis: Blue Steel treated as a non-capability
problems.claim: "Britain never fielded a stand-off round that worked. Blue Steel of 1963 reached about 100 nautical miles against an e60 area SAM this game gives 10.6 tiles, Skybolt was cancelled in December 1962 and Blue Streak in 1960, so there is no British `alcm_b` to write." And on the gbr_e60 card: "What it has no way of doing is releasing from outside the missile belt." And: "ASMP ... is the weapon Britain wanted and was refused."
problems.reality: Blue Steel was fielded, not cancelled — it is listed beside two cancelled programmes as if it were a third. Wikipedia (Avro Vulcan): "From 1963, three squadrons of Vulcan B.2s and two squadrons of Victor B.2s were armed with the Blue Steel missile." In service February 1963 (617 Sqn first, then 27 and 83; Victors 100 and 139), launched at ~100 nmi / 185 km, Mach 2.3–2.5, from 70,000 ft, 1.1 Mt Red Snow, the RAF's primary strategic weapon until the Polaris handover on 30 June 1969, withdrawn 1970. It is the Vulcan B.2's signature weapon for six of the e60 band's ten years, and the gbr_e60 card text is false for every one of them. The "inside the belt" argument is also refuted by the file being edited: heavyair.js already rates the C-601 at about 100 km as 8.6 tiles ("launched from about 100 km - which in 1986 was genuinely outside a task group's reach"), and this same proposal rates ASMP at 80–300 km as 10.4 tiles. Blue Steel's 185 km sits between those two anchors. Writing it as 2.2 tiles — identical to a free-fall bomb, identical to the 1955 Valiant — is not the compression the report defends, it is deletion. Britain was not "refused" a stand-off missile; Britain built one, then was refused its successor. Fix: a `bluesteel` round at roughly 8.5–9.5 tiles, `manual`, mounted on gbr_e60_heavybomber alongside yellowsun2 (a unit carries multiple mounts — nato_e80_gunshipair carries three). That also gives the British arc a real shape: reach in 1963, and back to overflying a runway in 1982.

problems.item: js/heavyair.js — gbr_e50 desc and file header: "the only V-bomber that ever bombed in anger"
problems.claim: Header: "the only V-bomber that ever bombed in anger, over Egyptian airfields at Suez in October 1956." Card: "The first of the three, and the only V-bomber that ever bombed in anger - Egyptian airfields, October 1956."
problems.reality: Contradicted by the row three entries below it in the same patch: gbr_e80_heavybomber "Vulcan B.2 (Black Buck)", whose own card says it was "sent 3,900 miles to bomb a runway" and put "one bomb of twenty-one" on Port Stanley. Wikipedia (Vickers Valiant): "It was the last time RAF V-bombers flew a live combat mission until Avro Vulcans bombed Port Stanley airfield in the Falkland Islands during the Falklands War in 1982." The Valiant was the FIRST V-bomber in combat and the only one used at Suez — not the only one ever to bomb in anger. A player reading the two cards in sequence sees the contradiction immediately.

problems.item: js/heavyair.js — ASMP range justification is arithmetically wrong
problems.claim: "10.4 tiles puts it just outside the 10.6-tile area SAM of e60 and just inside the 12.5 of e80, which is honest: a stand-off weapon against last decade's defences."
problems.reality: 10.4 is less than 10.6 — it is inside, not outside. Measured on the patched tree, the e60 maximum ground-based air-defence reach is exactly 10.6 (SP-HAWK / Bloodhound Mk 1, "first-generation area SAM"), and ASMP resolves at range 10.4 after the DOMAIN pass (only acc moves, 0.88 -> 0.898). Worse: entities.js:2150 sets `standoff = (w.proj === "missile" || w.antiRadiation) && !w.bomb` and then holds at `range * 0.88`, so the Mirage IVP actually shoots from 9.15 tiles — 1.45 tiles inside the e60 belt and 3.35 inside the e80 one. The sentence describes the opposite of what the numbers do.

problems.item: js/heavyair.js header — "the only airframe here that appears twice for two different jobs"
problems.claim: "VULCAN B.2 holds e60 AND e80 - the only airframe here that appears twice for two different jobs."
problems.reality: Refuted by the two paragraphs immediately above it in the file this text is being inserted into. heavyair.js opens: "The point of the Buff is that it changed job without changing airframe. In 1955 it was a nuclear bomber that had to fly over the target; over Vietnam it carried a hundred and eight iron bombs ... from 1982 it carried cruise missiles" — six B-52 rows across four jobs. And the H-6 header: "1969 is free-fall bombs over the target; 1986 is two enormous liquid-fuelled anti-ship missiles ... 2009 is a cruise-missile rail" — three rows, three jobs. The Vulcan is the only airframe appearing exactly twice; it is not the only one appearing more than once for different jobs.

problems.item: js/heavyair.js — Operation Grapple location, in the header and in the gbr_e50 player card
problems.claim: "the first British hydrogen bomb over Christmas Island on 15 May 1957" (header), and "the first British hydrogen bomb over Christmas Island on 15 May 1957" (gbr_e50 desc); sources block: "the first British hydrogen bomb over Christmas Island 15 May 1957 (Op Grapple)".
problems.reality: The 15 May 1957 Short Granite drop by Valiant XD818 (Wg Cdr Kenneth Hubbard) was over MALDEN Island, about 330 km south of Christmas Island; Christmas Island was the staging base, not the target. It also yielded about 300 kt against a predicted megaton. The first British true-megaton air drop was Grapple X on 8 November 1957 — and that one was near Christmas Island. The proposal has the two events' locations crossed, and the error is in text the player reads.

problems.item: js/heavyair.js gbr_e80 comment and sources block — Black Buck distance in the wrong unit
problems.claim: "XM607 flew 3,900 nautical miles from Ascension on 30 April 1982" / sources: "3,900 nmi each way".
problems.reality: Ascension to Stanley is 3,889 statute miles (6,259 km) ≈ 3,375 nmi; the round trip is the ~6,600 nmi / ~8,000 statute miles usually quoted. The card's own "sent 3,900 miles" is correct — it is the nautical version in the code comment and the sources block that inflates it by about 15%.

problems.item: js/heavyair.js gbr_e80 comment — XM607's squadron
problems.claim: "Black Buck 1, XM607 of 44 Sqn, Ascension, 30 April - 1 May 1982".
problems.reality: XM607 was on 44 Squadron's strength from July 1981, but the Black Buck 1 crew was Flt Lt Martin Withers's from 101 Squadron, and Wikipedia's Operation Black Buck captions the aircraft "Vulcan XM607 of 101 Squadron RAF". The Waddington Wing pooled aircraft and crews from 44, 50 and 101. Either attribution needs the qualifier; stated flat it credits the wrong unit with the sortie.

problems.item: js/heavyair.js — Valiant production total
problems.claim: "104 built" (sources block) and "104 built" in the header narrative.
problems.reality: 107 built per the Wikipedia infobox; the article states 108 manufactured including the sole B.2 prototype. 104 is the PRODUCTION total (36 B.1, 11 B(PR).1, 44 B(PR)K.1, 13 B(K).1). Say "104 production aircraft" — as written it reads as the type total and is three short.

problems.item: js/heavyair.js header — France "built the whole chain itself"
problems.claim: "the one nation here that built the whole chain itself: aeroplane, warhead, missile and the tanker doctrine to reach with it" — then, two sentences later, "France bought twelve C-135F the same year".
problems.reality: The tanker is a Boeing, bought from the United States, as the same paragraph says. And the claim is not uniquely French even on its own terms: Britain's chain at e60 was Vulcan + Red Snow + Blue Steel + Victor tanker, every link British. The sentence only survives because Blue Steel has been written out (see the fatal finding).

problems.item: report risks — "no AIRCRAFT in the roster has ever carried a held round before"
problems.claim: "the precedent is all GROUND launchers (every tel_*), and no AIRCRAFT in the roster has ever carried a held round before ... The three TEL rows prove the gate itself works; they do not prove it works from an airborne platform." Also: "`manual` is the flag the eleven held rounds already in the game use".
problems.reality: Measured on the patched tree: six aircraft already carry a `manual` round as their ONLY weapon — sead_n (F-16CJ Wild Weasel), sead_g (Tornado ECR), sead_c (J-16 SEAD), sead_p (Su-24M SEAD), ew_n (EA-18G Growler), ew_c (J-16D). entities.js:2053 even gives them a dedicated airborne self-release path: seadTarget() issues `{type:"attack", ..., release:true}` so a Weasel takes its own shot. The airborne precedent exists and is exercised. Separately, `manual` resolves to 41 weapons under jsc, not eleven — the report's own rule is that the source line is never the final answer.

problems.item: js/heavyair.js gbr_e80 — one raid standing in for the class's decade
problems.claim: gbr_e80_heavybomber carries `blackbuck` and nothing else; "an iron bomb needs no release authority".
problems.reality: From 1966 the Vulcan B.2's standing weapon was the WE.177B free-fall nuclear bomb, and that — not iron bombs — was the aeroplane's job right up to 1982. Modelling the 1980s Vulcan as conventional-only is the trap the brief names, inverted: one sortie's fit credited to the whole class for a whole era band. Defensible as a deliberate Black Buck snapshot, but neither the comment nor the card says WE.177 existed, so the reader takes the omission for the whole truth.

problems.item: report and three edits — "gbr_e60_tanker, Victor K.2, e60 to e80" as the Victor's answer
problems.claim: "What the Victor is in this game is what it became: gbr_e60_tanker, Victor K.2, e60 to e80." The same line is asserted in the heavyair.js header, the eras.js Britain block and the rules.js gbr e20 block.
problems.reality: Measured: gbr_e60_tanker is indeed named "Victor K.2", from e60 to e80. But the Victor K.2 did not enter service until May 1974 — the e60 tanker was the Victor K.1, converted from 1965 precisely because the Valiant tankers had just been grounded. The proposal did not introduce the mis-designation, but it now writes it into three files as the justification for leaving the Victor off the bomber rows. Either fix the tanker row (K.1 at e60, K.2 at e80) or drop the mark number from the new prose.

problems.item: js/heavyair.js sources — Victor B.2 and Blue Steel date
problems.claim: "B.2 with Blue Steel from Feb 1962".
problems.reality: 139 Sqn took the Victor B.2 (later B.2R) at Wittering from February 1962 and 100 Sqn from May 1962, but Blue Steel itself did not enter service until February 1963. The February 1962 date is the airframe's, not the weapon's.

problems.item: js/heavyair.js mirage4() comment — "faster than most fighters of its own decade"
problems.claim: "a two-seat Mach 2.2 delta ... by a wide margin the fastest aircraft in this file and faster than most fighters of its own decade."
problems.reality: First half true (7.6 against the next-fastest 4.9 in heavyair.js). Second half false as measured: every e60 fighter in the game is faster — Lightning F.6 8.6, MiG-21 7.92, J-6 7.83, Mirage IIIE 7.8, F-4 Phantom II 7.65. It is also not true in life: the Lightning, MiG-21, F-4 and Mirage IIIE were all Mach 2 class. Comparable, not superior.

missed: BLUE STEEL, as an omission rather than a misstatement: there is no `bluesteel` weapon and no mount for it, so the RAF's actual 1963-1970 strategic weapon does not exist in the game at all. Everything else in the V-force is modelled; this is the one thing that made the Vulcan B.2 a strategic bomber rather than a large aeroplane with a bomb in it.
WE.177B, the Vulcan's nuclear weapon from 1966 to 1982 and the reason the e80 row's aeroplane was still on QRA at all. The e80 row has no nuclear option and the comments never mention the weapon.

WHY THE VALIANT'S SPAR CRACKED, which is the proposal's own theme and it walks past it. The Valiant was taken off the high-level strategic role and assigned to SACEUR for LOW-LEVEL strike in 1962 because SAMs had made 50,000 ft untenable; low-level flying is what fatigued the rear spar, cracks were found on WP217 in August 1964, and the fleet went on 26 January 1965. The aeroplane was killed by the same shift in the threat that the whole British arc is supposed to be about, and the report treats the grounding as a maintenance accident.

The Mirage IVA's actual entry-into-service weapon. fra_e60_heavybomber is written `service: "1964"` and armed with the AN-22, which did not arrive until 1967; the AN-11 of 1964 is named in a code comment but the card presents a 1964 aeroplane with a 1967 bomb and says nothing.

France's e50 absence is the only EMPTY band in the patch that is not argued from a named aircraft. The Sud-Ouest Vautour IIB was in service from 1958 as France's jet bomber; the correct answer is still EMPTY for a STRATEGIC row, but every other absence in this patch gets its reason and this one gets only "no warhead until 1960".

Whether four of the five new rows can do anything without a human. gbr_e50, gbr_e60, fra_e60 and fra_e80 carry a single `manual` weapon, so allWeaponsHeld() is true and acquire()/retaliate() will never fire them; risk 1 worries the AI will BUILD them but never asks what an AI-built Vulcan does after it is built. The SEAD aircraft solve this with seadTarget(); a bomber has no equivalent, so an AI that builds one may fly a 3,400-cost airframe around with the safety on.

Blue Danube's Maralinga yield. The Operation Buffalo 'Kite' round of 11 October 1956 was deliberately reduced to about 3 kt, not the ~10-12 kt design figure the weapon comment quotes, and the card says only 'Britain's first atomic bomb' where the precise claim is Britain's first AIR-DROPPED atomic bomb (Hurricane, 3 October 1952, was detonated in a ship).
